additional_hardware.coverage: creation, enrollment, verification, sudo, restart persistence, and password fallback

findings.finding: Host endpoint numbers and internal service handles select distinct routes; raw Intel endpoint 16 reaches AMDM.
AKS has 0x48-byte v1 and 0x50-byte v2 envelopes; capability negotiation begins with v1.
Create-v5 returns a live handle and optional KEK material; operation 0x02 separately exports the reloadable keybag.
MacBookPro16,2 / J214K with bridgeOS 23P2048 uses an explicitly selected 76-byte create-v4 body; rewriting the version word of the 88-byte create-v5 body is invalid.
Creation flags 6 use the raw 16-byte ACM external reference as derivation input; save it before creation and supply it as type-5 data during later verification.
Operation 0x21 authorizes a distinct target; operation 0x18 carries the fresh input context reference while that target remains live.
Matched sks stores salt at bag +0xcc, work factor at +0xe0, and links credential records at +0x2a0; these are in-memory offsets.
AKS 0x51 suboperation 0 reads primary identity; definite absence is status -3 and does not recover a lost saved keybag.
The successful startup publishes typed EFI/SMC boot state and then establishes AKS application readiness.
sks durable loading sends internal command 0x271b through the xART service handle; xART constructs a master opcode-5 backing request.
Endpoint-16 status 0x2d came from unsupported AMDM command dispatch, correcting the earlier gigalocker-I/O interpretation.
Embedded PCI 106b:2002 namespaces differ from host ANS2 106b:2005; namespace type at Identify Namespace +0x180 differs from NSID.
First enrollment supplies the results needed to construct native user, master, and BioLockout archives without an imported prototype.
Restore master, selected user, and latest rolling BioLockout state; reconcile the selected account and actual identities.
Recorded results include cross-boot restore, positive and negative matching, exact deletion with survivor verification, and a continuous second-finger enrollment.
Installed native standard-fprintd first and additional enrollment, verification, selected deletion, durable rename, and automatic reboot reconciliation were exercised on the greenfield authority.
Immutable first-enrollment account proof must be paired with the reconciled current identity set and completed mutation history, without requiring the original fingerprint to remain enrolled.
Neutral names are five stable enrollment slots backed by private UUIDs; deleting one never renumbers survivors, and the next successful enrollment takes the lowest vacancy.
After SEP removed a selected identity, recovery supplied the committed master Catacomb and completed persistence without replaying the delete command, followed by reboot and survivor checks.
Direct D-Bus clients must handle service loss, latch completed results, and bound cleanup waits while preserving uncertainty about hardware completion.
A historical post-deletion addition was retained as finger-4 and survived reboot reconciliation; the product allocator was subsequently corrected to reuse the lowest vacant one of five stable slots.
Unattended biometric/fprintd startup and real sudo fingerprint authentication succeeded; a separate fprintd-unavailable transaction timed out biometric verification and accepted the Linux password.
